$comment: ★★★ LANE-CFG EDIT 3/4 — `includes: [{header: dirent.h, when: {format: pe}}]`, AND THIS IS A DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM BOTH REFERENCES. IT IS LABELLED AS ONE so a future lane meeting a green tree and a red probe can tell which won. ✔MEASURED: NEITHER reference makes `DIR` reachable from <direct.h> — MSVC `cl` rc=2, mingw rc=1 — against a `&_mkdir` control on the SAME header that compiles rc=0 on both, so the probe discriminates rather than merely failing. WE TAKE THE EDGE ANYWAY, as a DECLARED SUPERSET DEVIATION: DSS's pe headers make MORE visible at one named edge, which is compatible iff it never makes LESS available and never changes the meaning of anything already visible. ⚠⚠ THE JUSTIFICATION FIRST OFFERED FOR THIS EDGE WAS 'on Windows neither reference SDK ships a <dirent.h> at all', AND THAT IS HALF FALSE — recorded because the true half is what carries the argument and the false half would have rotted into folklore. ✔MEASURED: MSVC ships NO <dirent.h> (a bare `#include <dirent.h>` is rc=2, and a filesystem sweep of the Windows Kits and VC tool include trees finds none), but **mingw-w64 DOES ship its own** (mingw-runtime, public domain, `DIRENT.H (formerly DIRLIB.H)`), and it supplies `DIR`/`opendir` at rc=0. Since DSS claims `__MINGW32__`, mingw IS our reference — so this is a deviation from a reference that HAS the header, not gap-filling for a platform that lacks it. ★ WHAT ACTUALLY JUSTIFIES IT is narrower and survives that correction: on the mingw path sqlite's own `windirent.h` shim is INERT, its guard being `#if defined(_WIN32) && defined(_MSC_VER)` (windirent.h:22), while `ext/misc/fileio.c` includes windirent.h (quoted, its own file) + <direct.h> and NEVER <dirent.h> on that branch — so under a real mingw that TU cannot compile at all. <direct.h> is the directory header a Windows program already reaches for, and completing it is what lets DSS build the file instead of requiring every Windows consumer to carry its own reading-half shim. ⚠ DO NOT re-frame this as 'DSS pe is a third platform with its own header graph' — that framing was explicitly rejected: we claim `__MINGW32__`, and consuming code stays entitled to mingw's graph. COMPATIBILITY IS ASSERTED, NOT ASSUMED: `examples/c-subset/pe_direct_dirent_superset` witnesses by EXECUTION that a TU which never includes <windows.h> still compiles and runs, and that a user's own declarations — an incompatible `typedef int HANDLE;`, a private `struct DIR`, a `free_slots` function — still WIN over the newly-visible shipped ones. ⚠⚠⚠ AND THE COMPATIBILITY CLAIM IS NOT UNCONDITIONAL — MEASURED, AND IT REFUTES THE CHECK THIS EDGE WAS CLEARED ON. The clearing measurement was 'a TU that defines its own struct DIR compiles rc=0 WITH and WITHOUT the edges'. ✔RE-MEASURED against a no-edge tree identical to live in every other respect: a TU that includes <direct.h> and defines a COMPLETE `struct DIR { int marker; char tag[8]; };` is rc=0 WITHOUT the edges and **rc=1 WITH them**, `error[F_ShippedTypeIdentityConflict] … declares tag DIR (0 bytes / align 1) but this translation unit declares the SAME tag as a DIFFERENT layout (12 bytes / align 4)`. So clause (b) of the superset rule — never change the meaning of anything already visible — DOES fail for this one shape: after this edge, a pe TU including <direct.h> can no longer define its own complete `struct DIR`, which it could before and still can on mingw. THAT IS A REAL COST AND IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL: carrying a private `struct DIR` shim is exactly what sqlite's own windirent.h does. It does not sink the deviation — the collision is the ORDINARY consequence of <dirent.h> being in scope, identical on every format, and it fails LOUD rather than silently — but the honest statement is 'superset except for a complete redefinition of the DIR tag', not 'compatible'. ✔WHAT DOES HOLD, re-measured the same way: a user `typedef int HANDLE;` (4-byte int shadowing Win32's 8-byte void*) and a user `free_slots` function are rc=0 both with and without, and a FORWARD declaration `struct DIR;` is rc=0 both ways — only a complete conflicting definition collides. The corpus example asserts those three and deliberately omits the fourth, with the reason written at the omission. ⚠ MARGINAL, measured: from a 1+4 baseline this edge alone closes 24 of 65 `fileio.c` errors; leave-one-out from the full set, dropping it leaves 65. | ★ TF-C111 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION P3): `library.pe` is now ucrtbase.dll — moved with the whole co-state group (malloc/stdlib/string/stdio/io/errno/direct/process/sys-stat in ONE commit). Membership is `_getcwd`/`_wgetcwd`: passed a NULL buffer they ALLOCATE the result on the CRT heap for the caller to free, and they set errno on failure — both runtime-owned identities. All 8 symbols re-MEASURED as ucrtbase exports at TF-C111 (`objdump -p`); no renames were needed, and the msvcrt dumpbin ordinals quoted below are retained as the c98 provenance record, NOT as the current binding. | Neutral shipped <direct.h> (Microsoft CRT directory management) — c98 (Windows-host sub-arc, the 3-header F001A batch). shell.c includes it on the pe route in the fileio extension (~9848, the `#else` of the !_WIN32 guard) whose mkdir macro routes to fileio_mkdir -> `_wmkdir(b1)` (~9956) — the ONLY direct.h symbol the active amalgamation calls. The remaining seven ship as the obviously-paired trivial siblings: the narrow/wide couples of the classic direct.h set (_mkdir/_wmkdir, _rmdir/_wrmdir, _chdir/_wchdir, _getcwd/_wgetcwd) — _getcwd doubles as the corpus example's live-run witness (a cwd read needs no argv, which pe lacks until D-RUNTIME-PE-MAIN-ARGS). `availableObjectFormats:[pe]` — a Microsoft-CRT header fails loud on elf/macho. `library:{pe:msvcrt.dll}` — all eight are msvcrt.dll exports (verified via dumpbin /exports: _chdir 209, _getcwd 368, _mkdir 658, _rmdir 695, _wchdir 911, _wgetcwd 985, _wmkdir 995, _wrmdir 1012), NOT kernel32. SIGNATURES (Microsoft SDK direct.h/corecrt_wdirect.h): char* _getcwd(char*,int) — note the int maxlen (POSIX getcwd takes size_t; the CRT form is i32) and the char* return (the buffer, or NULL); int _mkdir(const char*) — NO mode param (unlike POSIX mkdir(path,mode); sqlite's mkdir macro drops the mode for exactly this reason); int _rmdir(const char*); int _chdir(const char*); the wide forms take/return wchar_t* — Windows wchar_t is UTF-16 u16 (== windows.json's WCHAR), so they spell ptr<u16> (same stddef.json wchar_t=i32 latent-width note as io.json).
